## PCI PM callback wiring

The PCI driver uses `i915_pm_ops` via `i915_pci_driver.driver.pm`:

- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_pci.c:1025-1032`
- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c:1714-1754`

There is **no function named `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`** in this tree. The runtime callback is named `intel_runtime_suspend`.

### Callbacks that reach `i915_pm_suspend`

Two PM-operation entries point directly to `i915_pm_suspend`:

```text
system suspend:
  i915_pm_ops.suspend
    -> i915_pm_suspend(kdev)
       -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)

hibernation poweroff:
  i915_pm_ops.poweroff
    -> i915_pm_suspend(kdev)
       -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
```

Locations:

- `.suspend = i915_pm_suspend` — `i915_driver.c:1719`
- `.poweroff = i915_pm_suspend` — `i915_driver.c:1745`
- `i915_pm_suspend()` — `i915_driver.c:1392-1405`

`i915_pm_suspend()` first returns early if the device is absent or already switcheroo-powered-off; otherwise it calls `i915_drm_suspend()`.

### Other PCI PM suspend-related callbacks

These are registered separately and do **not** call `i915_pm_suspend`:

```text
.prepare
  -> i915_pm_prepare
     -> i915_drm_prepare

.suspend_late
  -> i915_pm_suspend_late
     -> i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, false)

.suspend_noirq
  -> i915_pm_suspend_noirq
     -> i915_drm_suspend_noirq(&i915->drm, false)

.freeze
  -> i915_pm_freeze
     -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
     -> i915_gem_freeze(i915)

.freeze_late
  -> i915_pm_freeze_late
     -> i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, true)
     -> i915_gem_freeze_late(i915)

.poweroff_late
  -> i915_pm_poweroff_late
     -> i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, true)

.poweroff_noirq
  -> i915_pm_poweroff_noirq
     -> i915_drm_suspend_noirq(&i915->drm, true)
```

Thus, if “callers” means all PM callbacks that eventually invoke `i915_drm_suspend()`, the complete set is:

```text
i915_pm_suspend
i915_pm_freeze
```

`i915_pm_suspend` is reached through both `.suspend` and `.poweroff`.

## Which callers also call runtime suspend?

None of the callers above call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`, because that symbol does not exist in this source tree.

The runtime suspend callback is independent:

```text
i915_pm_ops.runtime_suspend
  -> intel_runtime_suspend(kdev)
```

Registered at:

- `i915_driver.c:1752`

`intel_runtime_suspend()` begins at `i915_driver.c:1545` and performs runtime-specific operations such as:

```text
intel_runtime_suspend(kdev)
  -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
  -> i915_gem_runtime_suspend(dev_priv)
  -> intel_pxp_runtime_suspend(dev_priv->pxp)
  -> ...
```

It is not called by:

- `i915_pm_suspend`
- `i915_pm_freeze`
- `i915_pm_suspend_late`
- `i915_pm_suspend_noirq`
- `i915_pm_poweroff_late`
- `i915_pm_poweroff_noirq`

## `dev_priv` data flow to display suspend

The actual display function is named `intel_display_driver_suspend`, not `intel_display_suspend`.

```text
i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
  |
  | i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
  |
  v
i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
  |
  | dev_priv = to_i915(dev)
  | display = dev_priv->display
  |
  v
intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
  |
  | state = drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm)
  v
DRM atomic display suspend
```

Relevant code:

```c
static int i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);
	...
	return i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm);
}
```

Then:

```c
static int i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);
	struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display;
	...
	intel_display_driver_suspend(display);
	...
}
```

Finally, in `display/intel_display_driver.c:684`:

```c
int intel_display_driver_suspend(struct intel_display *display)
{
	struct drm_atomic_state *state;
	int ret;

	if (!HAS_DISPLAY(display))
		return 0;

	state = drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm);
	ret = PTR_ERR_OR_ZERO(state);
	...
}
```

So `dev_priv` is not passed directly to the display layer. It is converted to `display` inside `i915_drm_suspend()`:

```text
kdev
 -> struct drm_i915_private *i915
 -> i915->drm
 -> struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv
 -> dev_priv->display
 -> display->drm
```
